# Context: reduction (jix/src/ops/reduction.rs)

Scope: `jix/src/ops/reduction.rs` lines 1-3404 (tests start at 3405). Written against commit
bb1ee2c. All line numbers below are in `jix/src/ops/reduction.rs` unless a file is named.

## Purpose

Lazy reductions over one or more dims: `Max`, `Min`, `ArgMax`, `ArgMin` (single dim), `Sum`,
`Product`, `Mean`, `Variance`, `StandardDeviation`, `All`, `Any`, and the user-closure `Reduce`
(`Array::reduce_unordered`). Each public op is a newtype over `ReductionOp<S, K>` (9-17) plus a
`ReductionOpKernel<T>` impl (trait 18-118). One generic driver (`read_data_impl`, 311-615)
streams the input in bulks/tiles and folds into per-output-cell states; the fold inner loops
(617-1115) pick one of several paths (one-cell vs multi-cell, contiguous/SIMD vs strided); a
finalize pass (1117-1259) turns states into outputs. Scalar-level traits (`jix::scalar::Sum`,
`Product`, `ArgMax`, `ArgMin`, `Mean`, `Variance`) live in `mod _traits` (1378-2032).
`Fold` (3093-3248) and `Array::fold` (3385-3402) are commented out - ignore them.

## Contracts

### Provided to callers

- `ReductionOp::new` (121-207): every dim must be `< ndim` and unique (129-139), else
  `InvalidArgument`. Order of dims is irrelevant (a bool mask). An empty dims list is legal and
  means "no reduction" (each cell = `finalize(init(x), 1)`). Kernels with
  `SUPPORTS_EMPTY == false` reject any reduced dim of extent 0 at construction (141-152). There
  are no negative dims and no keepdim in Rust (`DimsArg` is `usize`, ops/common.rs:81-89).
- Output shape = kept dims in original order (154-164). Output spec: block shape, fixed-dims,
  scale weights and `read_layout_order` filtered to kept dims and renumbered (166-198);
  `element_cost` multiplied by `reduced_prod + 4` (171); flags cleared (257).
- `read_data` (218-242 -> `read_data_impl`): standard pull/push contract. Every cell in `index`
  is written exactly once (by finalize, or in place when states live in `out` and
  `NEEDS_FINALIZE == false`). Empty output range returns before touching anything (395-398).
- Per-cell semantics (comment 345-393): stream = input elements with matching kept coords,
  row-major over reduced dims; `nitems` given to finalize is `full_reduction_size` (463-466), the
  product of the reduced extents - the same for every cell, never a per-state count.
- `Op::new` / `new_array` return `Err`; `Array::<op>()` methods `unwrap()` and panic
  (`#[track_caller]`, 3253-3286, 3377-3383).

### ReductionOpKernel contract (18-118) - provided by kernels, relied on by the driver

- `init_state(Some((item, idx)))` seeds a lane or a cell from its first item. `idx` is `Some`
  iff `NEEDS_INDICES` (default `true`!; `false` for Max/Min/Sum/Product/Mean/Var/Std/All/Any)
  and is the row-major position in the reduced sub-shape. `init_state(None)` is called only for
  empty reductions (1255), so only `SUPPORTS_EMPTY` kernels may see it; others `unwrap()`.
- `update_state` folds the next item of the SAME lane; lanes see items in ascending stream
  position. ArgMax/ArgMin `update` keeps the earlier item on ties (1638-1643) and relies on this.
- `merge_states` must be associative + commutative over disjoint subsets; used for lane
  collapse (1007-1026), the pairwise tree (902-908) and cross-tile merges in the one-cell path
  (803-806). ArgMax merge breaks ties by lower index (1646-1652).
- `NEEDS_FINALIZE = false` is an unsafe promise (92-99): `Output` has `State`'s layout and
  `finalize_state` is the identity. Claimed by Max 2106, Min 2183, Sum 2441, Product 2535,
  All 2891, Any 2958, Reduce 3075 (all `Output = State`, finalize returns `state`). Consumed at
  1145-1151. The trait is `pub(crate)`, so users cannot add kernels; `Reduce`'s `F` is user code.
- `PREFER_TREE_MERGE == false` folds a whole run as one leaf (889); `ONE_CELL_LANES` (111-113)
  is `Some(8 on x86 / 16)` for ArgMax/ArgMin (2267, 2349), else derived from SIMD width and
  `size_of::<State>()` (820-830, result in [8, 512]).

### Relied on from other modules

- `check_get_range` (error.rs:212) validates index ndim and bounds. `check_out_buf`
  (storage/buf.rs:282-297) checks ONLY stride count and writability - not length, alignment or
  aliasing. Those are the `unsafe` construction contract of a writable `StridedBuf`
  (buf.rs:78-117): in bounds, and no two indices map to the same byte (no 0-stride on a len>1
  dim). The state-in-out path (below) depends on that.
- `materialize_out_buf` (buf.rs:300-317): pull mode allocates from the pool at the output dtype
  alignment, strides = multiples of itemsize in layout order. Pool memory is UNINITIALIZED
  (util/buf_pool.rs:34-51), and so is the tmp state buffer (502). Every state must therefore be
  written (init) before any `assume_init_read`.
- `inner_array.read_data(tile, ctx, None)` (566): pull mode; returns bytes valid for `tile` at
  the inner's own usize strides, possibly 0-strides (broadcast), possibly unaligned
  (buf.rs:20-22), containing valid `T` bit patterns (a `bool` byte must be 0/1).
- `read_shape_heuristic` (storage/params.rs:728-750) -> `scale_read_shape` (util/mod.rs:468-526):
  scaled dims are clamped to `>= 1`; a dim whose read length equals its requested extent is
  snapped to `array_shape[d].max(1)` (may exceed the requested range). The driver divides by
  `tile_shape[d]` (440, 536) for every dim, i.e. assumes every dim is in the scale order.
- `calc_block_end` (util/mod.rs:609-617) and `NdIter` + `with_block_offset_size_ext`
  (util/iter/nd.rs:422-517): bulks/tiles partition `[begin, end)` exactly, in row-major order;
  a 0-dim `NdIter` yields exactly one item.
- `NdIterUnordered::new_with` (util/nd_iter_unordered.rs:62-170): drops len-1 dims; sorts by
  per-operand stride (operand 0 first; a 0 stride abstains; operand 2, the logical stream index,
  is excluded via `affects_dim_order`); coalesces only when ALL operands (including the logical
  one) agree; an all-len-1 region becomes shape `[1]` with strides = layout sizes (84-93); any
  len-0 dim gives shape `[0]`. Outer dims are walked in ascending order (261-299).
- `PtrNoalias` / `PtrMutNoalias` (util/mod.rs:657-760): `bytes_offset` requires
  `offset <= span`; the `noalias` tag must be truthful. `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` (util/mod.rs:641-645) is
  `false` on x86/x86_64/aarch64, `true` elsewhere (armv7, wasm).
- Scalar ops: integer `Add`/`Mul` wrap (ops/op2.rs:627, 635); `Maximum`/`Minimum` propagate a
  canonical NaN and may return either zero sign (ops/cmp.rs:13-121); `Cast` (ops/cast.rs:8-60,
  real-to-complex 169-180); `Sqrt` status (ops/op1.rs:576-603); `map_vectors2` falls back to
  scalar when `N` is not a multiple of the vector width (scalar/simd.rs:207-240).

## Unsafe inventory

- 498 `from_raw_parts_mut(out_ptr, out_buf_len)`: state buffer aliases the output bytes when
  `state_in_out_buf` (485-491: same itemsize, state align <= output align, base and all out
  strides multiples of output align). `out_buf` is not used afterwards (only ptr/len kept,
  492-493). Local, but correctness of later typed access relies on the out-buffer contract.
- 581-582 `get_unchecked_mut(state_offset..)`: needs `state_offset <= state_buf.len()`.
  NON-LOCAL: tile containment is only `debug_assert` (558-564); for the tmp buffer the length is
  `out_nitems * kernel_state_sizeof` (501, unchecked multiply); for out buffers it relies on
  the caller's StridedBuf span.
- 732-733 `bytes_offset(item_offset)` / `bytes_offset(state_offset)`: offsets come from
  `NdIterUnordered` over `tile_shape` with the items' and states' strides. NON-LOCAL: the inner
  storage's pull buffer must span its strides; the state buffer must span the output strides.
- 802-807 `&mut *ptr.cast::<MaybeUninit<State>>()`, then `assume_init_read` iff
  `base_item_idx > 0`: needs alignment (485-491 / 502; only `debug_assert` 704-708) and that the
  cell was initialized earlier in THIS call. NON-LOCAL: depends on visitation order (see Hot
  spots 1).
- 925 and 1090-1091 `assert_unchecked` on strides: 925 is established by the flags 712-716
  (`items_contiguous`: inner item stride == `size_of::<T>()`); in 1090-1091 the CONTIGUOUS
  strides are synthesized at 1070, so correctness rests on the flags 722-725
  (`items_contiguous && items_aligned && state_contiguous`). 1236-1237 is checked at 1201.
- 975-1001 item reads: CONTIGUOUS uses `read_maybe_aligned::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>` (an aligned read
  only when 699-701 verified base + all strides aligned); `[T; LANES]` reads (988-993) need
  `i + LANES <= len` (callers pass multiples of LANES); strided path uses `read_unaligned`.
- 1015-1025 lane collapse with `MaybeUninit`: each slot read once per level; "not panic-safe"
  (1012) - only `Reduce`'s user closure can panic, and State: Copy, so no double drop.
- 1098-1112 multi-cell: `&mut *states.add(i)` / `byte_add` (aligned reference) and
  `assume_init_read` when `!INIT`; `INIT` is decided by `base_item_idx == 0` at 640. NON-LOCAL.
- 1163-1165, 1175, 1242-1246, 1254-1257 finalize: raw pointer adds; `read_unaligned` of the state
  then `write_unaligned` of the output, possibly the SAME address (1241) - safe only because
  each element is read before it is written and strides are identical when aliased.

## Edge-case surface

- Empty reduced dim: only Sum/Product/All/Any. `bulk_grid_end` = `calc_block_end(0, 0, 1)` = 0,
  so no bulks run and `finalize_states` writes `finalize(init_state(None), 0)` to every cell
  (1171-1177). All other kernels error at `new` (141-152).
- Empty kept range: early return (395-398); test `reduction_empty_output_subrange`.
- All dims reduced: 0-d output, `out_nitems` = 1, state strides all 0 -> one-cell path.
- 0-d input: only `dims = []`; `InnerD = DimDyn` (289); NdIterUnordered single-element case.
- `dims = []`: `full_reduction_size` = 1; var gives 0 (ddof 0) or NaN (ddof >= 1).
- Single-element tile: NdIterUnordered reports state stride = state size and logical stride 1,
  so it takes the multi-cell path with len 1 (debug_assert 718-721 depends on `inner_len == 1`).
- Broadcast input (0 item strides) on reduced or kept dims; push `out` with permuted, gapped,
  unaligned base or non-multiple strides (falls back to tmp state + unaligned writes; tests
  `sum_into_misaligned_out_buf`, `sum_into_out_buf_with_unaligned_strides`,
  `sum_into_strided_2d_output_multi_bulk`, `var_into_strided_output_non_aliasing_state`).
- NDIM_MAX = 8: `InnerD` static for 1-4 dims, `DimDyn` otherwise (284-290).
- Alignment: on i686 u64/f64 align to 4; on armv7/wasm `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` is true.
- Dtypes: bool (Sum -> u64, Mean/Var -> f64, All/Any bool-only, no Product); f16 (Sum/Product
  accumulate in f16, Mean in f32, Var in f64, Max/Min scalar only); Complex (Sum, Product, Mean,
  Var, Std; no Max/Min/Arg*).
- Integer accumulators wrap silently: Sum/Product into i64/u64 (1487-1503, 1574-1581); Mean of
  i8..i32 sums in i64, of u8..u32/bool in u64, of i64/u64 in f64 (1740-1756).
- NaN/inf/-0.0: Max/Min canonical NaN; ArgMax/ArgMin first NaN; `Sum::init` is `-0.0` (1472) so
  a sum of `-0.0`s stays `-0.0`; Variance of `inf` is NaN; `ddof = NaN` gives NaN.
- 32-bit targets (x86, armv7 wheels): u64 -> usize at 335, 395, 477, 501, 570, 575-578, 580 and
  in `item_idx` (971). Reduced extents > 2^32 are reachable with lazy broadcasts or
  highly-compressible Compact arrays.

## Intentional behaviors

- Integer sum/product/mean-sum wrap on overflow and report no `ArithmeticOpStatus` (docs
  1419-1422, 1507-1510; commit 98b2ed3 "Wrap integers sum, product and mean").
- `sum(bool)` -> u64 (NumPy int64) and `product(bool)` unsupported (2368-2369, 2462-2463;
  jix-py/python/tests/test_reduction.py:524-528, 616).
- Accumulation width: Sum/Product keep the input width for floats/complex (f16 sum accumulates in
  f16; Rust tests skip f16 sum, comment at 4063); Mean widens (f16 -> f32, f32 -> f64,
  Complex<f32> -> Complex<f64>, i64/u64 -> f64; 1740-1756); Var/Std accumulate in f64 for all
  real inputs and return the real component type for complex (1959-2031, 2625-2628).
- Reassociation: lane count, pairwise tree and tile merges depend on SIMD level, shape, block
  shape and read size; float results differ in the last bits between paths (2975-2990,
  101-109). Float Product is never tree-merged (2536). Variance's bulk path multiplies by
  `1/count` (1944-1947) while the scalar path divides (1840): last-ulp differences are expected.
- Max/Min propagate NaN (2037-2039, 2114-2116) as the canonical NaN, either zero sign for +-0
  (ops/cmp.rs:24-27). ArgMax/ArgMin return the first NaN and the earliest index on ties
  (1594-1597, 2193-2196); output u64; single dim only (multi-dim argmax is reachable only by
  building `ReductionOp` directly, crate-internal - see test
  `multi_dim_argmax_reports_the_true_stream_position`).
- Empty reductions: Sum -> 0 (2370), Product -> 1 (2464), All -> true (2833), Any -> false
  (2900); Max/Min/ArgMax/ArgMin/Mean/Var/Std/Reduce -> `Err` from `new`, panic from the
  `Array` method (141-152, 2994-2996). The Mean doc says "panics" (2547) - only the `Array`
  method panics.
- Var/Std with `n - ddof <= 0` -> NaN (1896-1904, 2632-2633), even where NumPy gives inf.
- Negative dims, `dim=None`, keepdim exist only in Python (jix-py/src/ops/reduction.rs:7-23,
  65-72; jix-py/src/util.rs:170-207); keepdim re-inserts with NumPy-style `InsertDim` positions.
- `reduce_unordered` closures must be associative + commutative (2975-2990); there is a test
  that each cell does exactly `n - 1` closure calls (each item folded exactly once).

- Kernels that need indices (ArgMax / ArgMin) assert they run over a single reduced dim (K41).

### Changed in 6f8e220 (#88) and 7e93487 (#89) - supersedes conflicting statements above

## Hot spots

1. Init vs merge is keyed ONLY on the stream position: `init = base_item_idx == 0` (640) for
   multi-cell, `base_item_idx > 0` -> merge with the stored state (803) for one-cell. Is there
   any layout where a cell's first visit has position > 0 (then `assume_init_read` of
   uninitialized pool memory - UB) or a later visit has position 0 (state overwritten, items
   lost)? Consider: reduced dims of length 1, broadcast reduced dims, reduced dims whose memory
   order is the reverse of their logical order, out buffers with permuted strides, tiles that
   start mid-extent on a kept dim, the single-element special case.
2. One-cell vs multi-cell is decided by `state_inner_stride == 0` (712). Can the inner run ever
   mix a reduced and a kept dim after coalescing, or be a kept dim with state stride 0 (e.g.
   a push `out` with a 0 stride on a len>1 dim - forbidden by contract, but is it ever created
   internally)? In release the debug_assert 718-721 is gone and argmax indices would be wrong.
3. Stream positions: `tile_base_reduced_idx` (573-578), the per-run base from the logical
   operand (735), lane indices + `idx_step` (929-955), tail indices (865). Do ArgMax/ArgMin pick
   the first max across lanes, tails, pairwise halves and tiles, with NaN anywhere?
4. `state_in_out_buf` (485-491) plus the in-place finalize (1145-1170): is every kernel that
   passes the size/align test safe to finalize in place (Mean<f64>, Mean<i8..u32>: i64/u64 state
   into f64 output)? Does the early return at 1145 ever skip a needed write?
5. Contiguous vs strided vs SIMD paths must agree: contiguous one-cell uses
   `K::ONE_CELL_LANES` or the SIMD-derived count (820-830), strided one-cell always 16 (799);
   multi-cell contiguous uses runtime SIMD dispatch (1071), strided uses baseline (1053).
6. Variance (recent rewrite, adef94b, only concrete tests): `welford_update_bulk` (1933-1957)
   vs scalar `update` (1836-1844); complex split into re/im passes sharing `m2` (1916-1930);
   `merge_states` with count 0 (1870-1875); finalize uses `nitems`, not `state.count` (1896).
7. Kernel seeds: `init_state(Some(x))` is `init op x`, not `x` (2411-2417, 2505-2511,
   2588-2594). Exact for real floats, not for complex (see Suspicions).
8. Size arithmetic on 32-bit targets (list in Edge-case surface).

### Suspicions (unverified)

- reduction.rs:1471-1473 + 1249-1259 - empty float/complex `sum` writes `Sum::init()` = `-0.0`
  (sign bit set); docs (2370) and NumPy give `+0.0`.
- reduction.rs:1732-1734 - complex `mean` divides `Complex / Complex(n, 0)` (num-complex uses
  `(a*c + b*d)/|c|^2`, `b*c - a*d`), so an infinite component makes the other component NaN
  (`inf * 0`): mean([inf+0j]) = (inf, NaN); NumPy divides by a real count -> inf+0j. Also `a*n`
  can overflow where `a/n` would not.
- reduction.rs:1557-1559 + 2505-2511 - complex `product` seeds with `(1+0i) * x`: for
  x = 1+inf*i this is (NaN, inf), so a product over a length-1 dim is not `x`; similarly
  `(-0.0+0i) + x` (1472) flips an imaginary `-0.0` to `+0.0` in `sum`.
- reduction.rs:573-578 - `tile_base_reduced_idx` is computed in usize: on 32-bit, argmax over a
  reduced dim longer than 2^32 (lazy broadcast / compressible Compact) truncates the index;
  `logical_stride *=` at 477 overflows (debug panic) for multi-dim reductions > 2^32 items.
- reduction.rs:501 - `out_nitems * kernel_state_sizeof` is unchecked; on 32-bit, with state
  larger than output (ArgMax 16B vs 8B, Var<Complex> 32B vs 8B) and a large push-mode `out`, the
  tmp buffer size wraps and 581/732 index past it.
